definitions.returnRate: Returns as a share of orders PLACED in this period — both halves counted the same way, so it agrees with the RETURNED count in Order outcomes. A cohort rate: of what was ordered here, how much came back.
definitions.refundValue: Refunds that flowed out DURING this period, whenever the order was placed. A deliberately different window from Return rate above — 'what did we pay out this month' and 'how much of this month's orders came back' are different questions, and one figure cannot answer both.

definitions.totalRevenue: Total money taken from orders placed in this period. Canceled orders are excluded — they never took money. Returned orders are NOT excluded: the money moved and then came back, which is a different fact from a sale that never happened. Each order contributes the total recorded when it was placed, so editing a price today never rewrites past revenue.
definitions.todaySales: Money taken from orders placed today at this branch. Canceled orders are excluded — they never took money.
definitions.todayOrders: Every order placed today at this branch, including canceled ones.
definitions.grossProfit: Revenue minus cost of goods sold, over the order lines that have a cost recorded. Lines with no recorded cost are left out entirely rather than counted as pure profit, so this is a partial figure — the note underneath says how much of the period it covers. Cost is the one captured at the time of sale, not the product's cost today.
definitions.grossMarginPercent: Gross profit as a share of revenue, measured only over the order lines that have a recorded cost — including revenue from uncosted lines would inflate it. Shown as a dash when no line in this period has a cost recorded, because that is unknown, not zero.
definitions.totalOrders: Every order placed in this period, INCLUDING canceled ones. An order that was placed and then canceled did happen; it simply realized no money, which is why it still counts here but not in Revenue.
definitions.canceledOrders: Orders canceled in this period. They are counted in Orders but excluded from Revenue, so these two tiles can legitimately move in opposite directions.
definitions.lowStockProducts: Products at or below the low-stock threshold RIGHT NOW. Unlike the other tiles, this ignores the selected date range — stock has a current level, not a history. Uses the threshold set in Settings, so it always agrees with the Inventory page.

definitions.revenue: Total money taken from orders placed in this period. Canceled orders are excluded — they never took money. Returned orders are NOT excluded: the money moved and then came back, which is a different fact from a sale that never happened. Each order contributes the total recorded at the time it was placed, so editing a product's price today never changes past revenue.
definitions.orders: Every order placed in this period, INCLUDING canceled ones. This deliberately differs from the denominator behind Average order — an order that was placed and then canceled did happen, it just realized no money.
definitions.averageOrderValue: Revenue ÷ orders, excluding canceled orders. The Orders tile counts every order including canceled ones, so the two intentionally use different denominators. Averaging in orders that realized nothing would understate what a real order is worth.
definitions.newCustomers: Customers whose record was created in this period — first-time customers, not everyone who ordered. A returning customer who ordered twice this month is not counted here at all.
definitions.canceledOrders: Orders canceled in this period. These are counted in Orders above but excluded from Revenue, which is why the two tiles can move in opposite directions.
definitions.lowStockProducts: Products at or below the low-stock threshold RIGHT NOW. Unlike every other tile here, this is a live snapshot and ignores the selected date range — stock has no history in a report sense, only a current level. The threshold is the one set in Settings, so this always agrees with the Inventory page.

guide.title: Admin guide
guide.heroTitle: Run the dashboard without waiting for a developer
guide.heroDescription: Follow the operating flows below to configure the brand, launch branches, publish products, connect the storefront, manage staff, and recover from common problems safely.

start.title: Start here
start.summary: Open the correct workspace directly. What you can see still follows your role and branch assignment.

templates.title: Understand what a setup template prepares
templates.summary: Business templates are starting presets. They configure the dashboard but do not create a finished business or industry-specific workflow.
templates.restaurantStatus: Selecting Restaurant prepares a generic POS and administration workspace. It can support a manually configured counter-service, takeaway, or pickup operation, but it is not a turnkey full-service restaurant system.
templates.homeBusinessTitle: Home business: a lean workspace without shop-floor clutter
templates.homeBusinessStatus: Selecting Home business starts with orders, delivery, inventory, reports, products, customers, discounts, and one home location. POS, suppliers, returns, customer cases, staff, and scheduled reports start hidden. You can change every choice, and hiding a feature never deletes its data.
templates.homeBusinessChecklist: Open the Home business launch checklist

applies.features: Feature visibility for dashboard, POS, tickets, inventory, suppliers, reports, team, branches, and settings.
applies.labels: Restaurant-friendly labels such as Menu items, Tickets, and Team.
applies.defaults: A small set of product and inventory defaults, including inventory variants.

missing.data: Branches, categories, menu items, prices, images, stock, staff, and branch assignments.
missing.modifiers: Sellable sizes, modifiers, add-ons, and meal customisation; current variants are inventory-only.
missing.tables: Tables, floor plans, seats, reservations, tips, and service charges.
missing.kitchen: Kitchen display, preparation stations, courses, and printer routing.
missing.recipes: Recipes, ingredients, allergens, BOM, and automatic ingredient depletion.

templates.nextStep: Complete the Restaurant readiness checklist before accepting a real sale. If the business depends on any missing workflow, treat it as product work rather than configuration.

brand.title: Set up the brand and branches
brand.summary: Complete this once for the brand, then repeat the branch-specific steps whenever a new location opens.

steps.profile: In Settings, enter the trading name, logo, currency, contact details, and customer-facing identity.
steps.branches: Create each real location with a unique code, city, active timezone, and selling-point status.
steps.tax: Confirm the tax rate and receipt information before processing a real sale.
steps.staff: Invite the Owner first, then assign branch-scoped staff to the branch where they actually work.
steps.verify: Sign in with a non-owner test account and confirm it sees only its permitted areas and branches.

brand.warning: A branch timezone controls daily reports and schedules. Choose the real local timezone; changing it later changes how dates are grouped.

catalogue.title: Build a sellable catalogue
catalogue.summary: A product is not ready merely because its record exists. It needs content, a price, active status, and branch stock.

steps.categories: Create the category tree first so products appear in the correct storefront and dashboard groups.
steps.products: Create each product with a unique SKU or barcode, tax-exclusive price, cost when known, and ACTIVE status only when ready. Leave Charge VAT on this product enabled for standard-rated goods; disable it only for an exempt or zero-rated product.
steps.stock: Add a branch-stock row for every branch that carries the product, then record the opening quantity through inventory.
steps.content: Add English and Arabic names and descriptions, verify the primary image, and review any missing translation indicators.
steps.preview: Check the product in the selected branch and confirm price, image, category, quantity, and sold-out behavior.

catalogue.stockRule: Branch membership is explicit: no branch-stock row means the branch does not carry the product. A row with quantity zero means the branch carries it but it is sold out.

storefront.title: Connect one brand website to every branch
storefront.summary: The website is brand-wide, while the customer-selected branch controls catalogue availability, stock, and fulfilment.

steps.key: Create a new key in Settings → API keys. Give it a clear name, purpose, and recipient.
steps.scope: Select only products, categories, discounts, and orders. Never leave a storefront key unscoped.
steps.store: Copy the key once into the storefront server's secret environment. Never place it in browser code or a NEXT_PUBLIC variable.
steps.branch: Request the active branch list, let the customer select a location, and store that branch ID in the storefront session.
steps.products: Fetch products or the menu with branchId on every catalogue request. Reload and revalidate the cart when the branch changes.
steps.checkout: Send the same branchId at checkout. The backend rechecks stock, price, discounts, and branch ownership before creating the order.
steps.retry: Generate one UUID Idempotency-Key for each checkout. Reuse it only while retrying the identical request; create a new UUID if any checkout or customer data changes.

storefront.never: The browser calls your storefront server. Only that server sends X-API-Key to the dashboard API. Revoke any key that appears in chat, logs, screenshots, or source code.

operations.title: Run daily operations
operations.summary: Use the same sequence every day so stock, cash, fulfilment, and audit history remain trustworthy.

opening.title: Open the day
opening.description: Select the correct branch, start the cashier shift, verify the opening drawer, review low stock, and confirm printers or scanners before the first sale.

sale.title: Process a sale
sale.description: Scan or browse branch-carried products, verify quantities and tender, submit once, and keep the receipt or order number for any later correction.

fulfillment.title: Fulfil orders
fulfillment.description: Work the branch queue in order, update status only when the physical step happened, and assign delivery work only to a courier serving that branch.

return.title: Handle returns
return.description: Open the original order, confirm remaining returnable quantity, record a reason and resolution, and verify stock and refund history afterwards.

closing.title: Close the day
closing.description: Resolve pending orders and returns, reconcile till takings, record drawer events, close the shift, and review exceptions before leaving.

access.title: Manage staff access
access.summary: Access follows both the staff role and branch assignment. Hiding a menu item is not the security control; the API enforces every request.

steps.invite: Create or invite the staff account using the person's own email address.
steps.branch: Assign branch-scoped roles to every branch where the person is expected to work.
steps.role: Choose the narrowest role that supports the person's duties; do not use Owner as a shortcut.
steps.review: Use View as role and a real test login to confirm the resulting navigation and refused actions.
steps.remove: When someone leaves, deactivate access, revoke sessions and API keys, then review recent audit activity.

access.rule: API keys act as their owner's permissions narrowed by the selected scopes. Deactivating the owner invalidates their keys immediately.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshoot common API failures
troubleshooting.summary: Use the response status and message to fix the request instead of repeatedly retrying it.

400.meaning: The branch ID or request body is missing or invalid.
400.action: Select a real active branch and check every required checkout field.

401key.meaning: The integration key is missing, invalid, revoked, or owned by an inactive account.
401key.action: Send X-API-Key exactly, or create and deploy a replacement key.

401customer.meaning: A customer-only route such as order history was called without a shopper token.
401customer.action: Send the customer's Bearer token or use the public catalogue route.

403.meaning: The key owner or selected scopes do not permit this area.
403.action: Grant only the required scope and confirm the owner already has that permission.

404.meaning: The branch or product is unavailable in the selected context.
404.action: Check active selling status, product ACTIVE status, and the branch-stock row.

429.meaning: Too many requests were sent in a short period.
429.action: Stop immediate retries, wait, then use backoff and caching where safe.

security.title: Security and recovery
security.summary: Treat credentials, production data, and migration history as operational assets. Recovery must be planned before an incident.

items.keys: Keep API keys server-only, minimally scoped, named by recipient, and revoke unused or exposed keys immediately.
items.accounts: Require individual accounts and two-factor authentication for privileged roles; never share an Owner login.
items.backups: Take restorable database backups before migrations or destructive maintenance, and test restoration in isolation.
items.audit: Review audit and login history after sensitive changes, refusals, suspicious access, or staff offboarding.
items.production: Never run development migrations, demo seeding, or test suites against the production database.
items.incident: If exposure is suspected: contain access, rotate credentials, revoke sessions, preserve request IDs, inspect audit history, and verify recovery.

checklists.title: Detailed operating checklists
checklists.subtitle: Reusable checklists for setup, branch launches, daily work, storefront integration, incidents, and production release.
checklists.resetDescription: This removes all saved ticks from this browser. It does not change dashboard data.

setup.title: Initial business setup
setup.description: Complete once before real staff or customer activity begins.

owner.label: Activate the customer Owner
owner.detail: Use the Owner's real account and remove temporary operator ownership when it is no longer required.

profile.label: Complete the brand profile
profile.detail: Verify trading name, logo, contact details, locale, and customer-facing identity.

currency.label: Confirm currency and money formatting
currency.detail: Check dashboard, storefront, receipts, and reports use the same approved currency.

tax.label: Confirm tax settings
tax.detail: Verify the rate, calculation order, receipt display, and one known-value example.

notifications.label: Configure operational notifications
notifications.detail: Set recipients and test in-app alerts; configure email only when every SMTP value is ready.

security.label: Harden privileged access
security.detail: Enable two-factor authentication, store backup codes safely, and review active sessions.

homeBusiness.title: Home business launch
homeBusiness.description: Complete after selecting Home business. The preset removes unused administration; this checklist prepares the remaining workflow for real orders.

profile.label: Complete the customer-facing profile
profile.detail: Set the trading name, logo, contact channel, currency, tax rate, pickup address, and the hours when customers can expect a reply.

location.label: Configure one home location
location.detail: Create or review the home branch, choose its real timezone, keep it active only when accepting orders, and use its ID for catalogue and checkout requests.

catalogue.label: Publish a small, complete catalogue
catalogue.detail: Create every sellable item with a clear name, price, tax behavior, image, availability, and English and Arabic content where required.

inventory.label: Choose how inventory will work
inventory.detail: Keep Inventory enabled and record opening quantities for stocked goods, or disable it in Business setup when every item is made-to-order or non-stocked.

delivery.label: Define pickup and delivery promises
delivery.detail: Document service areas, fees, address requirements, preparation time, handoff steps, failed-delivery handling, and the person responsible for each order.

customers.label: Verify customer records and consent
customers.detail: Capture only necessary contact details, prevent duplicates, and record valid email or SMS marketing consent before sending promotions.

discounts.label: Test discounts before publishing
discounts.detail: Confirm code, dates, limits, eligible products, branch behavior, tax calculation, and one rejected and one accepted checkout example.

orders.label: Run the complete order workflow
orders.detail: Create an order, confirm it, prepare it, assign delivery or pickup, complete it, and verify stock, customer history, totals, and notifications at every step.

acceptance.label: Complete a real-device acceptance run
acceptance.detail: Place English and Arabic test orders from a phone, test sold-out and invalid-discount cases, complete delivery and pickup, then verify the dashboard and reports.

restaurant.title: Restaurant readiness
restaurant.description: Complete after selecting Restaurant. The template is a starting preset; this checklist turns the configured workspace into a tested counter-service operation.

serviceModel.label: Confirm the supported service model
serviceModel.detail: Use the current system for counter service, takeaway, or pickup. Record any need for tables, reservations, courses, tips, or kitchen display as product gaps before launch.

menu.label: Build the complete menu
menu.detail: Create categories and every sellable item with approved English and Arabic names, prices, costs, tax behavior, images, and ACTIVE status.

options.label: Model sizes and add-ons safely
options.detail: Current variants are inventory-only and cannot be purchased in POS or storefront checkout. Create separate products for each sellable option or postpone launch until modifier support exists.

stock.label: Assign menu stock by branch
stock.detail: Create a branch-stock row and opening quantity for every sellable menu item at every branch that carries it.

team.label: Configure the restaurant team
team.detail: Create individual staff accounts, select the narrowest roles, assign branches, and verify each role through View as role and a real test login.

pos.label: Configure and test the POS
pos.detail: Verify shifts, opening cash, tenders, discounts, receipts, printers, scanners, voids, refunds, split payment, and closing reconciliation.

fulfilment.label: Define pickup and delivery operations
fulfilment.detail: Confirm order statuses, pickup handoff, delivery areas, courier assignments, address requirements, and failed-delivery handling.

storefront.label: Connect the customer website
storefront.detail: Keep the API key server-side, implement branch selection, load the branch menu, revalidate carts after branch changes, and test English and Arabic.

payments.label: Confirm the payment model
payments.detail: Cash and card-on-delivery labels do not create an online gateway. Integrate and test a real provider before advertising online card payment.

acceptance.label: Run a full restaurant acceptance day
acceptance.detail: Open a shift, sell each option, print receipts, verify stock, complete pickup and delivery, process a void and return, close the till, and review branch-local reports.

branch.title: New branch launch
branch.description: Repeat for every physical location or selling point.

identity.label: Create the branch identity
identity.detail: Use a unique name and code and verify the city and business relationship.

timezone.label: Set the real local timezone
timezone.detail: Daily reports, audit buckets, notifications, and schedules depend on this value.

selling.label: Confirm active selling-point status
selling.detail: Only active selling branches should appear to the public storefront.

staff.label: Assign the branch team
staff.detail: Add each branch-scoped staff member and verify their effective role.

stock.label: Load opening stock
stock.detail: Create branch-stock membership and record quantities through traceable inventory movements.

test.label: Run a branch acceptance sale
test.detail: Test catalogue visibility, POS checkout, receipt, stock decrement, order detail, and daily reporting.

catalogue.title: Catalogue readiness
catalogue.description: Use before publishing products or connecting a storefront.

categories.label: Review category structure
categories.detail: Remove duplicates, confirm parent relationships, and keep customer-facing names clear.

products.label: Review product identities
products.detail: Confirm unique SKU/barcode, status, category, and searchable name for every sellable item.

prices.label: Verify price, VAT, and cost
prices.detail: Confirm every price is tax-exclusive, set Charge VAT on this product correctly for each item, and record cost where margin reporting is expected. Test a basket containing both taxable and exempt goods.

images.label: Verify product imagery
images.detail: Confirm a primary image, ordering, crop quality, and useful alternative text.

translations.label: Review English and Arabic content
translations.detail: Check names, descriptions, SEO content, bidi behavior, and missing-translation fallbacks.

branchStock.label: Assign products to branches
branchStock.detail: Create stock rows only for branches that carry each item and confirm the exact quantity.

soldOut.label: Test sold-out behavior
soldOut.detail: A carried item at zero must show sold out; an uncarried item must not appear for that branch.

storefront.title: Storefront/API connection
storefront.description: Complete for the one brand website and repeat key rotation checks when credentials change.

key.label: Create a dedicated storefront key
key.detail: Name the recipient and purpose clearly so the credential can be identified later.

scopes.label: Limit the key scopes
scopes.detail: Grant only products, categories, discounts, and orders as required by the storefront.

secret.label: Store the key server-side
secret.detail: Use a secret environment variable; verify the key never reaches browser code or logs.

branches.label: Load and select branches
branches.detail: Call the branch endpoint, present a location choice, and persist the selected branch ID.

catalogue.label: Test two branch catalogues
catalogue.detail: Confirm the same product can report different stock and an uncarried item stays hidden.

languages.label: Test English and Arabic
languages.detail: Send Accept-Language and verify content, RTL layout, and fallback behavior.

idempotency.label: Prove checkout retry safety
idempotency.detail: Repeat the identical checkout with the same UUID Idempotency-Key; confirm the original order is returned and stock is reduced only once.

guestOrder.label: Place a guest order
guestOrder.detail: Verify totals, branch ownership, stock decrement, order visibility, and tracking.

customerOrder.label: Test a signed-in customer
customerOrder.detail: Verify profile, cart, wishlist, checkout link, and order history using both credentials.

rotation.label: Prove key rotation
rotation.detail: Deploy a replacement, verify it, revoke the old key, and confirm the old key immediately returns 401.

opening.title: Daily opening
opening.description: Complete before the first order or till sale of the day.

branch.label: Confirm the selected branch
branch.detail: Verify the shell, reports, till, and inventory are all operating in the intended location.

shift.label: Start the cashier shift
shift.detail: Use the correct staff account and confirm the shift is attached to the right branch.

drawer.label: Record opening cash
drawer.detail: Count the drawer and record discrepancies before processing sales.

devices.label: Check till equipment
devices.detail: Verify scanner, printer, network, payment equipment, and receipt paper.

stock.label: Review stock exceptions
stock.detail: Check low-stock and sold-out items and correct only through recorded movements.

alerts.label: Review pending work
alerts.detail: Check returns, failed deliveries, notifications, and orders needing attention.

closing.title: Daily closing
closing.description: Complete before the final shift closes.

orders.label: Resolve open orders
orders.detail: Confirm every status matches the physical fulfilment state and document exceptions.

returns.label: Resolve pending returns
returns.detail: Approve, reject, or leave a clear note with an accountable next owner.

deliveries.label: Reconcile delivery work
deliveries.detail: Review active assignments, failed attempts, courier cash, and unreturned orders.

cash.label: Count and reconcile the drawer
cash.detail: Compare expected and actual cash and record drops, payouts, or variances.

shift.label: Close and review the shift
shift.detail: Generate the report, close the till, and obtain approval where policy requires it.

exceptions.label: Review the day timeline
exceptions.detail: Check unusual refunds, voids, stock adjustments, access refusals, and unresolved alerts.

staff.title: Staff onboarding and offboarding
staff.description: Use for every person who receives dashboard access.

invite.label: Use an individual identity
invite.detail: Invite the person's own email; never create a shared team login.

role.label: Select the narrowest role
role.detail: Match actual duties and avoid Owner or Developer access as a convenience.

assignment.label: Assign permitted branches
assignment.detail: Confirm branch-scoped roles have every required branch and no unrelated branch.

activation.label: Complete first login
activation.detail: Have the user set their password, accept policies, and verify the expected navigation.

twoFactor.label: Enable two-factor authentication
twoFactor.detail: Require it for privileged users and store backup codes outside the browser.

review.label: Review access periodically
review.detail: Check roles, assignments, active sessions, keys, and recent login history.

offboard.label: Offboard immediately
offboard.detail: Deactivate the account, revoke sessions and keys, reassign work, and inspect audit history.

incident.title: Security incident response
incident.description: Use when a key, password, session, device, or production credential may be exposed.

contain.label: Contain access
contain.detail: Disable the affected account or integration and stop unsafe automated traffic.

revoke.label: Rotate exposed credentials
revoke.detail: Create safe replacements, update approved services, and revoke old keys or passwords.

sessions.label: Revoke active sessions
sessions.detail: Remove unrecognized sessions and require affected users to authenticate again.

audit.label: Inspect audit and login history
audit.detail: Establish what happened, which areas were reached, and the first and last suspicious time.

evidence.label: Preserve safe evidence
evidence.detail: Record request IDs, timestamps, account IDs, and actions without copying secrets or customer PII.

restore.label: Verify recovery
restore.detail: Test normal access, confirm old credentials fail, monitor for recurrence, and document prevention.

release.title: Production go-live
release.description: Final gate before exposing a release to real customer data and operations.

commit.label: Approve the exact commit
commit.detail: Use a clean, reviewed commit with green required checks and known ownership.

backup.label: Take and test a backup
backup.detail: Restore it into isolation and record the timestamp, checksum, operator, and result.

migrations.label: Verify migration history
migrations.detail: Check names, checksums, status, generated client, and guarded production deployment.

builds.label: Run the full quality gate
builds.detail: Complete backend and frontend typecheck, lint, tests, and production builds from the lockfile.

bilingual.label: Review English and Arabic
bilingual.detail: Check translations, RTL, bidi values, typography, overflow, and a native Arabic review.

accessibility.label: Complete accessibility checks
accessibility.detail: Verify keyboard flow, focus visibility, semantic headings, contrast, and mobile touch targets.

acceptance.label: Run end-to-end acceptance
acceptance.detail: Test auth, branches, catalogue, POS, orders, inventory, returns, delivery, reports, settings, and audit.

monitoring.label: Confirm operational monitoring
monitoring.detail: Verify health checks, logs, alert routing, uptime ownership, and support contacts.

rollback.label: Confirm rollback readiness
rollback.detail: Name the rollback owner and last known-good commit and verify database recovery constraints.
